item.title: Mother calls for transparent investigation into alleged rape of 13-year-old as Police continue investigations
item.description: A concerned mother is calling for a transparent and thorough investigation after her 13-year-old son was allegedly raped by six senior students at a school in Lautoka, with Police investigating the matter. Speaking to fijivillage News, the mother alleges the incidents occurred over several months, from last year until October this year.
item.content:encoded:
A concerned mother is calling for a transparent and thorough investigation after her 13-year-old son was allegedly raped by six senior students at a school in Lautoka, with Police investigating the matter.

Speaking to fijivillage News, the mother alleges the incidents occurred over several months, from last year until October this year.

She says she reported the matter to Police last month after learning about what had allegedly been happening to her son.

The mother claims the students had threatened her son, warning him that if he reported the alleged abuse to teachers, it would tarnish his reputation and that of his family.

She says her son is not attending school as the alleged incidents have left him traumatised and fearful for his safety.

She says the incident has also emotionally affected her son, who is not eating well and has become unusually quiet.

The mother is calling for immediate action and a transparent investigation to ensure her son receives justice and is protected.

She says no child should have to fear going to school or suffer abuse when they are simply there to receive an education.

Meanwhile, Police have confirmed to fijivillage News that they have received the report and interviewed two suspects, while investigations are continuing to determine whether others were involved.

We have sent further questions to Police.

item.title: Dry conditions leave farmers unable to grow vegetables in Tavua, price of vegetables double in Ba
item.description: Due to the prolonged dry weather conditions, Ahsan Ali has been forced to buy and resell vegetables to maintain his livelihood. Ba Market vendor Ali, who lives in Vatia, Tavua, says conditions in his area are very dry and vegetable prices have more than doubled.
item.content:encoded:
Due to the prolonged dry weather conditions, Ahsan Ali has been forced to buy and resell vegetables to maintain his livelihood.

Ba Market vendor Ali, who lives in Vatia, Tavua, says conditions in his area are very dry and vegetable prices have more than doubled.

Ali says the situation has drastically affected vegetable prices, with okra (bhindi) now selling for $7 per kg, eggplants costing $50 per bag and cucumbers also selling for $50 per bag.

He says the high prices are making it difficult for vendors and consumers.

Ali says families in his area are also experiencing water issues, although they are fortunate to have a borehole that provides water for their daily needs.

However, he says the borehole water is used for drinking and not sufficient for farming.

Ali says this is the first time he has experienced vegetable prices reaching such high levels.

item.title: Charters' application for leave to seek judicial review set for hearing on 23rd December
item.description: The hearing of Charlie Charters' application for leave to seek judicial review has been set for 23rd December. Charters claims that Prime Minister, Sitiveni Rabuka's advice and the President, Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu's appointment of Lavi Rokoika in May 2025 were unlawful and ultra vires (beyond legal authority), arguing that the recommendation power rests solely with the Judicial Services Commissi
item.content:encoded:
The hearing of Charlie Charters' application for leave to seek judicial review has been set for 23rd December.

Charters claims that Prime Minister, Sitiveni Rabuka's advice and the President, Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu's appointment of Lavi Rokoika in May 2025 were unlawful and ultra vires (beyond legal authority), arguing that the recommendation power rests solely with the Judicial Services Commission after consulting the Attorney-General.

He says because of the alleged unlawful appointment, a Stop Departure Order issued against him on February 21st, 2026, and criminal charges sanctioned by Rokoika on February 23rd, 2026, were void of legal authority.

Charters is claiming special, general, vindicatory, aggravated, and exemplary damages against FICAC and Rokoika (representing the State) for alleged false imprisonment following his 48-hour detention from February 21st to 23rd, misfeasance in public office, and constitutional breaches under Sections 13 and 17 of the Fiji Constitution.

The matter was called before Justice Dane Tuiqereqere in the Suva High Court this morning.

item.title: Confidential bullying reporting mechanism proposed for schools
item.description: A recent bullying case at Queen Victoria School involving Year 13 students allegedly bullying 37 Year 11 students, has raised questions about the monitoring and reporting of bullying incidents in schools. The issue was raised in Parliament by Opposition MP Hem Chand, who questioned why the Ministry of Education was informed of the incident by parents rather than the school head.
item.content:encoded:
A recent bullying case at Queen Victoria School involving Year 13 students allegedly bullying 37 Year 11 students, has raised questions about the monitoring and reporting of bullying incidents in schools.

The issue was raised in Parliament by Opposition MP Hem Chand, who questioned why the Ministry of Education was informed of the incident by parents rather than the school head.

Chand says the case highlights weaknesses in the monitoring and reporting of bullying incidents and asked what the Ministry is doing to ensure such matters are reported promptly.

Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro says the incident was handled according to the Ministry's existing policies and procedures, with the only discrepancy being the delay in reporting the matter to the Ministry.

Radrodro says the Ministry maintains a zero-tolerance approach to bullying and has policies in place to guide schools in preventing, reporting and managing such incidents.

These include the Student Code of Conduct, Behaviour Management Policy, Child Protection Policy and Drugs and Substance Abuse Policy.

He says school heads are responsible for receiving complaints, establishing the facts, ensuring the immediate safety of affected students, involving parents and guardians where appropriate, providing counselling and support, and applying corrective or disciplinary measures.

Radrodro says serious incidents involving physical assault, abuse or threats to students' safety must be reported promptly to the Ministry and referred to relevant authorities, including the Fiji Police Force where necessary.

He also urged school heads not to conceal or delay reporting serious incidents, saying timely information allows the Ministry to intervene and protect students.

Meanwhile, Opposition MP Premila Kumar questioned whether the Ministry would consider establishing an independent and confidential reporting mechanism that would allow students to report bullying directly to the Ministry without fear of retaliation.

Kumar says students may face further bullying if their complaints are not handled confidentially, while some may also be reluctant to report incidents for fear of offending school authorities.

In response, Radrodro says the Ministry is reviewing its existing policies to address the concerns raised.

Opposition MP Vijay Nath a lso asked whether the Ministry could provide Parliament with the total number of bullying cases reported this year, broken down between primary and secondary schools.

Another proposal was raised in Parliament for Fiji to consider introducing specific legislation to address bullying in schools, similar to the approach taken in Northern Ireland.

Radrodro says the Ministry is also considering establishing a national school safety and anti-bullying steering committee.

He says the Ministry wants to explore a system requiring schools to provide reports periodically to ensure timely reporting and better monitoring of incidents.

Radrodro says the Ministry will not rule out the suggestions raised in Parliament as it continues to review ways to address bullying in schools.
